# GridEconomics daily - Thu 1 Oct 2026

**Headline.** Greece: negative-price hours at 7 h, higher than on 92 % of its last 90 days.

**Price decoupling.** The widest price gap between connected zones was Sweden (Malmö, SE4) and Lithuania: baseload 159.4 against 50.1 €/MWh, 69 % apart, with prices split in 24 of 24 hours. In coupled markets prices only separate when the cross-border capacity is fully used, so the border was the bottleneck in those hours. Next: Poland and Lithuania (66 % apart).

**Next 24 h.** Tomorrow's auction puts Romania at the widest TB4, 256.1 €/MWh (peak 316.1 at 19:00 CET, low 11.7 at 13:00). Negative hours expected in Greece.

**Fundamentals (last 30 days).** Wind output covered the largest share of load in Lithuania (51.7 %), Germany-Luxembourg (30.2 %), Greece (24.8 %). Solar did in Greece (34.9 %), Bulgaria (34.7 %), Lithuania (24.3 %). Across 16 zones the rank correlation of the wind + solar share with negative hours is +0.29 and with the mean TB4 -0.02.

_Data notes: No complete day-ahead price day for Bosnia and Herzegovina. No wind and solar shares for Romania: generation or load data is late._

30-day window ending on the brief's day. Wind = onshore + offshore. Share of load = output / actual load (energy). CF = mean output / the highest hourly output in the last 90 days (a proxy for installed capacity, so it reads higher than a nameplate capacity factor). Capture rate = output-weighted day-ahead price / mean day-ahead price.

Prices €/MWh. TB2/TB4: mean of the 2/4 highest minus 2/4 lowest hourly day-ahead prices of the CET day. Source: ENTSO-E Transparency Platform.
